I looked at the spreadsheet you described. It records one row per loan (Seed, Packets, Borrower, Date out, Date back), and about a third of the "Date back" cells are empty. That blank column is probably the most useful clue about what's going wrong. It could mean several different things, and each would lead to a different tool.

Something specific to seed libraries also bears on this. Often nobody returns the packet they borrowed. They grow the plant, save seed at the end of the season, and bring back seed from their own harvest, sometimes months later and sometimes a different amount. If that's how yours works, "lent out" and "come back" are separate events, and a library-book style checkout tool would be the wrong shape.

So I'd like to understand what an empty "Date back" means to you, because that decides what the tool needs to track. When you see one of those blank cells, what's usually happened, and what do you wish you could do about it?
